name: The Lodge at Primland, Auberge Collection
positioning: The Lodge at Primland is a Blue Ridge Mountains resort in Virginia on 12,000 private acres above the Dan River Gorge, with a lodge, cottages, Tree Houses and mountain homes.
best_for: Travelers who want a secluded mountain stay with golf and outdoor activities
Guests who like the idea of sleeping in a Tree House

facts.text: The Lodge at Primland sits on 12,000 private acres above the Dan River Gorge in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia.
The Lodge rooms and suites have deep soaking tubs, private balconies, sliding floor-to-ceiling windows and Frette sheets.
Fairway Cottages sit along the golf course and have cathedral ceilings and living areas with Tennessee fieldstone fireplaces.
Eleven Rustic Mountain Homes at the Sporting Club have wraparound decks, outdoor hot tubs and stone fireplaces.
The Highland Course is an 18-hole championship golf course set across the ridges and valleys of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
The Primland Sporting Club offers sporting clays, archery and air rifle, with guides and instruction.
Leatherflower is the main restaurant and offers a culinary journey through the tastes of Appalachia.
Stables Saloon serves a Southern supper family-style.
Sage, Wellbeing by Auberge, is the resort's spa and wellbeing destination, inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains.
The indoor heated swimming pool is chlorine-free.

highlights.text: The Tree Houses were designed in France by the treehouse architectural firm La Cabane Perchee and built of aromatic red cedar.
The Schlumberger Wine Cellar in The Lodge is named for the sister property Domaines Schlumberger in Alsace, France.
Stables Saloon is on the second floor of Primland's former horse stables, regularly hosts live bluegrass concerts and is part of the Crooked Road: Virginia's Heritage Music Trail.
The resort has an on-property observatory, and Condé Nast Traveler describes nightly guided stargazing sessions there.
The Junior Mountaineers Kids Club is for children ages 6-12 and includes pond-fishing, foraging, archery and horseback riding.

considerations.text: Accessing the Tree Houses requires a four-wheel drive vehicle, and complimentary shuttle services are available for guests without one.
Condé Nast Traveler says guests who want to go off property would need a car of their own.
Private airport transportation is available for a fee upon request.
